findings.reason: a done node is treated as delivered, so the coordinator builds s3/s4/s6 on a context wiring that the plan's own later section proves absent.
findings.text: s2 is declared done, but its done-when requires that the case file "is the single thing the reference set, the benchmark and generation read, none of them collecting the same text again"; s8 (§s8) records that the case file "is imported by nothing in the pipeline: every stage still assembles its own context and none is checked" — verified in the tree, where only tests/standard_names/test_case_file.py imports iter_codex.standard_names.case_file and no pipeline stage does

findings.reason: s6 regenerates equilibrium with the same ad-hoc context whose absence the plan names as the root cause, so the group is regenerated against the unchanged defect.
findings.text: s8 finds that every stage assembles its own context and defers supplying the missing channels to "the sections that own the prompts", but names none, and no section delivers it: s2 (done) claimed the wiring, and s3, s4 and s6 consume generation without any of them owning a channel; the enclosing-structure omission the plan blames for equilibrium's defects is therefore left unowned

findings.reason: a done-when that its own cited measurement shows unreachable cannot close the section and will be reported as a failed gate every time it is attempted.
findings.text: s3 requires "two control arms ... must separate" and "a benchmark in which neither control separates is reported as measuring nothing", but the committed second-round scores carry incumbent 54 right against the best repairing arm 59 on the 79 members both scored (difference 0.063, 95 % interval −0.013 to 0.139, called_win false), so the incumbent control does not separate and s3 as written can never be delivered; the first round already reported measuring=false for the same reason

findings.reason: the control's defect is an arithmetic consequence of the reference set's defect share, so the fix is a different control, not more rounds with this one.
findings.text: s1's premise that "at least 20 [defective members] ... so a generator that copies the incumbent scores below one that repairs it" is used to justify the incumbent control, but a 47-of-176 defective share leaves the incumbent right on 129 of 176, and the measured held-out figures in benchmark-second-round-scores.json show the repairing arms do not separate from it

findings.reason: a node built from s3 implements a control the lead has already removed, and the ruled replacement appears nowhere in the section it governs.
findings.text: the plan's own comment of 2026-11-20 records the lead ruling replacing the withheld-text control with one that moves the answer, and round one reported the withheld control "unmeasurable once restricted to members the full arm answered correctly"; s3 still specifies the withdrawn control as a requirement

findings.reason: "final figures once on the held-out half" can no longer be honestly produced from that half, so the protocol needs a fresh held-out set or a recorded statement that the half is spent.
findings.text: s3 remains implementable and requires "the final figures being taken once on the held-out half", but the second round's figures already come from the 87 held-out members (benchmark-second-round-scores.json reports 87 members per arm; s7 states the same), so the held-out half has been read and is no longer held out

findings.reason: as declared, s7 waits on the census it does not use and is released without the benchmark evidence it translates, so the queue either holds it needlessly or admits it against work that has not landed.
findings.text: the dependency table gives s7 depends-on [s8] only, yet s7's endpoint rests on the reference set's held-out members and their committed blind verdicts (s1) and on the second-round defect classes (s3); nothing in s7 consumes a context receipt

findings.reason: s9 can be admitted on an unreceipted stage census while the group it reads has not been regenerated, and the cross-plan resumption it promises has no ordering behind it.
findings.text: s9 declares depends-on [s8], but its families are "each family of the first group", which s6 is the section that regenerates, and it resumes a family re-render held on sn-definitions-by-construction; neither relationship is declared

findings.reason: the stated conclusion that the difference is inside the interval holds either way, so the miscited denominator changes no decision.
findings.text: s7 states the incumbent "right on 54 of 87 held-out members and the best regenerating arm on 60", but the cited file gives 60 of 78 scored for that arm, and head-to-head on the common members 59 of 79
